page7_img_1.png.title: Normalized defect density by clone group size (Apache & Gimp, conservative/liberal)
page7_img_1.png.description: The figure contains four side-by-side boxplots (Apache conservative, Apache liberal, Gimp conservative, Gimp liberal) that compare normalized defect density (buggy cloned lines ÷ total cloned lines) for clone groups of size ≤3 versus >3. In every panel the median and interquartile range for large (>3) groups are much lower and tighter than for small (≤3) groups, while the small-group category shows a higher median, a much wider spread and numerous high-value outliers (values occasionally exceed 1.0 because a clone group can contribute buggy lines for multiple bugs). These patterns hold for both conservative and liberal DECKARD settings and, as reported in the paper (Table III), the differences are statistically significant by Wilcoxon tests.

page6_img_1.png.title: Clone-ratio boxplots: snapshots vs bugs for Apache and Gimp
page6_img_1.png.description: Four side-by-side boxplots compare the distribution of clone ratio (y-axis 0.0–0.4) in project snapshots versus in buggy code: Apache (conservative), Apache (liberal), Gimp (conservative), and Gimp (liberal). In all subplots the median clone ratio for staging snapshots is visibly higher than the median for buggy code (e.g., Apache medians ≈0.06–0.09 for snapshots vs ≈0.0–0.02 for bugs; Gimp snapshots ≈0.12–0.15 vs bug medians ≈0.05), and the bug distributions show a wider tail of outliers (some bugs with clone ratios up to ≈0.35–0.4). As discussed in the paper, this visual pattern (persistent across conservative and liberal DECKARD settings) reflects a statistically significant lower clone ratio in buggy code compared to the overall snapshot clone ratio.

page5_img_table2.png.title: Adjusted p-values for Wilcoxon tests comparing snapshot vs bug clone ratios
page5_img_table2.png.description: The table lists Benjamini–Hochberg–adjusted p-values from paired Wilcoxon tests (alternative hypothesis: snapshot clone ratio > bug clone ratio) for four projects under conservative and liberal clone-detection settings. Numeric results are: Apache — 3.777e-05 (conservative), 3.3e-04 (liberal); Evolution — 1.291e-04, 9.4e-05; Gimp — 6.482e-06, 2.2e-05; Nautilus — 3.394e-06, 1.1e-03. All adjusted p-values are well below conventional significance thresholds (most <0.001), providing strong evidence that the overall snapshot clone ratio is higher than the clone ratio found in buggy code across projects and detector settings.

page5_img_figures.png.title: Cumulative bug coverage vs. clone ratio for Apache and Gimp
page5_img_figures.png.description: Two cumulative distribution plots (Apache left, Gimp right) show the fraction of bugs whose fixed code has clone ratio ≤ x (x on the horizontal axis). Red circles are bug coverage using the conservative DECKARD setting and green X’s the liberal setting; vertical dashed lines (red and green) mark the overall average clone ratio across snapshots for each setting. In both projects the curves climb steeply near zero: roughly 70–85% of bugs have very little or no cloned code, and the snapshot-average clone ratio is to the right of this steep rise, indicating that cloned code is a smaller fraction of buggy code than it is of the project as a whole. The conservative detector yields slightly higher bug clone ratios than the liberal setting, but both curves reach 1.0 as clone ratio approaches 1.0.

page6_img_table_1.png.title: Adjusted Wilcoxon p-values for projects (conservative vs liberal clone detection)
page6_img_table_1.png.description: A three-column table listing four projects (Apache, Evolution, Gimp, Nautilus) with adjusted p‑values from Wilcoxon tests under two DECKARD parameterizations labeled “p‑value (Conservative)” and “p‑value (Liberal)”. The reported values are: Apache: 6.666e-03 (conservative), 4.850e-12 (liberal); Evolution: 1.418e-05, 4.400e-16; Gimp: 8.800e-16, 4.400e-16; Nautilus: 1.000e-02, 8.900e-03. In the paper’s context these are Benjamini–Hochberg–adjusted p‑values from paired Wilcoxon tests (alternative hypothesis: snapshot clone ratio > bug clone ratio), and all entries are below common significance thresholds, indicating statistically significant differences for both conservative and liberal clone-detection settings across the four projects.

page5_img_table1.png.title: Project size and clone statistics for Apache, Evolution, Gimp, and Nautilus
page5_img_table1.png.description: A numeric summary for four C projects showing repository scale, monthly snapshot counts, clone metrics (under conservative and liberal DECKARD settings) and number of linked bugs. Rows report: Apache (155 snapshots, ~124.5K lines per snapshot, ~13.8K cloned lines conservatively / 16.6K liberal, clones/group ≈3.2, lines per clone ≈14.8, 453 linked bugs), Evolution (129 snapshots, ~324.5K lines, ~26.3K / 33.0K cloned, clones/group ≈2.5, ≈15.3 lines/clone, 1,440 bugs), Gimp (130 snapshots, ~755.5K lines, ~167.2K / 176.1K cloned — the highest clone volume and proportion, clones/group ≈3.4, ≈22 lines/clone, 2,103 bugs), and Nautilus (116 snapshots, ~131.1K lines, ~14.9K / 17.5K cloned, clones/group ≈2.2, ≈18 lines/clone, 747 bugs). The liberal detector setting (similarity relaxed to 0.99) increases cloned-line counts modestly for all projects; clone-group sizes and average lines-per-clone remain in the ~2.2–3.4 and ~15–22 range respectively.
